title: From Ricci curvature to ball volume, with six companion comparisons
audience: A first-year doctoral reader who can differentiate maps on smooth manifolds, use orthonormal bases and trace/determinant, solve elementary ODEs and use basic integration. Connection calculus, Jacobi tensors and global comparison geometry are established or precisely imported here, not assumed from a previous course.
reader_goals: Recognize the full hypotheses and conclusions of all seven classical comparison interfaces.
Explain why sectional curvature controls individual radial directions while Ricci controls relative volume expansion.
Reproduce the radial differential, Gram density, shape operator, singular trace comparison, cut substitution, weighted average and positive-curvature endpoint.
Identify the first failed step after changing curvature direction, cut restrictions, completeness or simple connectivity.
prerequisites: Smooth-manifold differentials; finite-dimensional symmetric matrices, trace and determinant; elementary ODE existence/uniqueness and Taylor expansion; change of variables and dominated convergence; the fundamental theorem for absolutely continuous functions.
